# Overview

This guide describes the implementation of the Bayesian continual
reassessment method (CRM) used in the accompanying manuscript. It covers:

- generation of true dose-response parameter values;
- specification of the Bayesian dose-response model;
- simulation of one illustrative CRM trial;
- posterior updating after each cohort;
- prior-predictive evaluation;
- evaluation under five fixed dose-response scenarios; and
- generation of operating-characteristic summaries, tables and figures.

The primary focus of this guide is the Bayesian CRM. The complete implementation
of the rule-based comparator is also provided in the accompanying repository.
Computationally intensive simulation code is displayed but is not run when this document is rendered. Saved simulation outputs are used to reproduce selected tables and figures.

# Software requirements

The analyses were conducted using R and Stan.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages

library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(rstan)
library(truncnorm)
library(kableExtra)
```

# Dose-response model

The probability of infection at challenge dose \(d\) is modelled using the
beta-Poisson dose-response relationship

\[
p(d)
=
1-
\left(
1+\frac{d}{b}
\right)^{-a},
\]

where \(a>0\) and \(b>0\) are model parameters.

The dose associated with a target infection probability \(p_T\) is

\[
ID_{p_T}
=
b
\left\{
(1-p_T)^{-1/a}-1
\right\}.
\]

The target infection probability in this study is

\[
p_T=0.70,
\]

so the target infectious dose is denoted by \(ID_{70}\).

# Candidate doses and design settings

Five candidate challenge doses are available:

\[
10^3,\ 10^4,\ 10^5,\ 10^6,\ 10^7
\quad\text{CFU}.
\]

The CRM starts at \(10^4\) CFU and enrols cohorts of five participants.

```{r}
#| label: common-design-settings

target_prob <- 0.70

target.doses <- 10^(3:7)

designs <- tibble::tibble(
  start.dose = 10^4,
  group.size = 5
)

N_cap <- 35

seed.no <- 250909
```

# Prior specifications

Two prior specifications are available.

## Primary prior

The primary specification places priors on \(a\) and
\(\log_{10}(ID_{70})\):

\[
\log(a)
\sim
\operatorname{Uniform}
\{
\log(0.3),\log(0.8)
\},
\]

and

\[
\log_{10}(ID_{70})
\sim
N(4,0.8^2),
\]

truncated to the interval \((3,7)\).

## Alternative prior

The alternative specification places independent log-uniform priors on
\(a\) and \(b\):

\[
\log(a)
\sim
\operatorname{Uniform}
\{
\log(0.1),\log(0.7)
\},
\]

and

\[
\log(b)
\sim
\operatorname{Uniform}
\{
\log(20),\log(600)
\}.
\]

```{r}
#| label: prior-settings

id70_settings <- list(
  a_lower = 0.3,
  a_upper = 0.8,
  log10_id70_mean = 4,
  log10_id70_sd = 0.8,
  log10_id70_lower = 3,
  log10_id70_upper = 7
)

ab_settings <- list(
  a_lower = 0.1,
  a_upper = 0.7,
  b_lower = 20,
  b_upper = 600
)
```

# Dose-allocation rules

After each completed cohort, the Bayesian model is updated using all infection
outcomes observed so far.

At the most recently administered dose:

- the dose is increased by one \(\log_{10}\) level if the 25th posterior
  percentile of the infection probability is below 0.60;
- the dose is decreased by one \(\log_{10}\) level if the 5th posterior
  percentile is above 0.80;
- otherwise, the dose remains unchanged.

An accelerated escalation may be applied when the posterior modal
\(ID_{70}\) category is above the initially proposed dose. Any escalation is
restricted to no more than two \(\log_{10}\) dose levels between consecutive
cohorts.

# Stopping criteria

The capped design stops when either:

1. 20 participants have been challenged at the dose administered to the most
   recently completed cohort, including participants challenged at that dose
   earlier in the trial; or
2. the maximum total sample size of 35 participants is reached.

The uncapped design applies only the first stopping criterion.

# Compile the Stan model

Select one of the two prior specifications.

```{r}
#| label: select-prior

prior_spec <- "id70_p"
```

The corresponding Stan model is selected and compiled as follows.

```{r}
#| label: compile-stan-model
#| eval: false

stan_file <- switch(
  prior_spec,
  id70_p = "crm_dr_id70_prior.stan",
  ab_p = "crm_dr_ab_prior.stan"
)

compiled_model <- rstan::stan_model(
  here::here(
    "bayesian_crm",
    "stan",
    stan_file
  )
)
```

Model compilation is not performed when this guide is rendered because it can
take several minutes.

# Illustrative simulated trial

This section illustrates the sequential operation of the Bayesian CRM using
one simulated trial.

The example uses Scenario 4 and simulation replicate 45 under the primary
prior specification.

## Run the illustrative trial

```{r}
#| label: run-illustrative-trial
#| eval: false

prior_spec <- "id70_p"
cap_method <- "capped"

example_scenario <- 4
example_sim <- 45

stan_file <- switch(
  prior_spec,
  id70_p = "crm_dr_id70_prior.stan",
  ab_p = "crm_dr_ab_prior.stan"
)

compiled_model <- rstan::stan_model(
  here::here(
    "bayesian_crm",
    "stan",
    stan_file
  )
)

example_output_folder <- here::here(
  "bayesian_crm",
  "results",
  "examples",
  paste0(
    "scenario_",
    example_scenario,
    "_sim_",
    example_sim,
    "_",
    prior_spec,
    "_",
    cap_method
  )
)

example_results <- run_bcrm_example(
  scenario_no = example_scenario,
  sim_no = example_sim,
  prior_spec = prior_spec,
  target_prob = target_prob,
  id70_settings = id70_settings,
  ab_settings = ab_settings,
  cap_method = cap_method,
  N_cap = N_cap,
  seed.no = seed.no,
  start.dose = 10^4,
  group.size = 5,
  target.doses = target.doses,
  compiled_model = compiled_model,
  chains = 4,
  iter = 3000,
  warmup = 1000,
  save.output.to = example_output_folder
)
```

The code is displayed but is not executed during rendering. The posterior
summaries saved from the illustrative trial are read below.

## Dose-allocation sequence

```{r}
#| label: example-dose-sequence

prior_spec <- "id70_p"
cap_method <- "capped"

example_scenario <- 4
example_sim <- 45

example_output_folder <- here::here(
  "bayesian_crm",
  "results",
  "examples",
  paste0(
    "scenario_",
    example_scenario,
    "_sim_",
    example_sim,
    "_",
    prior_spec,
    "_",
    cap_method
  )
)

trial_dat <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(
    example_output_folder,
    "learning_trial_dat.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

trial_sequence_table <- trial_dat %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Cohort = cohort,
    `Dose (CFU)` = ds,
    `Number infected` = obs,
    `Cohort size` = nn,
    `Observed infection proportion` =
      round(obs / nn, 2)
  )

knitr::kable(
  trial_sequence_table,
  caption = "Dose-allocation sequence for the illustrative simulated trial."
)
```

## Posterior updating after each cohort

```{r}
#| label: fig-posterior-updating
#| fig-cap: "Updating of the posterior dose–infection relationship after each completed cohort."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6

post_curves <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(
    example_output_folder,
    "learning_post_curves.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

scenario_parameters <- readr::read_csv(
  here::here(
    "data",
    paste0(
      "pars_scenarios_",
      prior_spec,
      ".csv"
    )
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

posterior_updating_plot <-
  create_fig_posterior_updating(
    trial_dat = trial_dat,
    post_curves = post_curves,
    true_a =
      scenario_parameters$a[
        example_scenario
      ],
    true_b =
      scenario_parameters$b[
        example_scenario
      ],
    id70_settings = id70_settings,
    target_prob = target_prob,
    n_cohorts_to_plot = 5
  )

posterior_updating_plot
```

The shaded bands show the pointwise 50% and 90% posterior credible intervals
for the infection probability. The green dashed line shows the true
dose-response relationship used to simulate the trial. Numbered points show
the observed infection proportions in successive cohorts.

# Prior-predictive evaluation

The prior-predictive evaluation assesses operating characteristics across a
broad range of possible true dose-response relationships.

One true parameter set is generated for each simulated trial, and 1,000
simulated trials are evaluated under each design and capping setting.

## Generate random true parameter values

```{r}
#| label: generate-random-parameters
#| eval: false

prior_spec <- "id70_p"
generation_method <- "random"

# Run data_gen/generate_parameters.R using:
#
# prior_spec <- "id70_p"
# generation_method <- "random"
# n_sim <- 1000
```

The resulting parameter file is saved as:

```text
data/pars_random_id70_p.csv
```

## Run prior-predictive CRM simulations

```{r}
#| label: run-prior-predictive-crm
#| eval: false

prior_spec <- "id70_p"
generation_method <- "random"
cap_method <- "capped"

bcrm_results <- run_bcrm(
  cap_method = cap_method,
  generation_method = generation_method,
  prior_spec = prior_spec,
  target_prob = target_prob,
  id70_settings = id70_settings,
  ab_settings = ab_settings,
  N_cap = 35,
  n_random = 1000,
  n_sim_scenario = 1000,
  seed.no = seed.no,
  designs = designs,
  target.doses = target.doses,
  compiled_model = compiled_model,
  chains = 4,
  iter = 3000,
  warmup = 1000,
  save.output.to = here::here(
    "bayesian_crm",
    "results",
    "bcrm_id70_p_random_capped"
  )
)
```

## Obtain operating-characteristic summaries


# Five fixed-scenario evaluation

Five representative dose-response scenarios are selected at the 5th, 25th,
50th, 75th and 95th percentiles of the prior-generated distribution of
\(\log_{10}(ID_{70})\).

One thousand simulated trials are evaluated under each fixed scenario.

## Generate fixed scenarios

```{r}
#| label: generate-fixed-scenarios
#| eval: false

generation_method <- "scenarios"
```

# Rule-based comparator

The primary focus of this implementation guide is the Bayesian CRM. The
simulation study also includes the conventional 5+5+10 rule-based design as a
comparator.

The complete implementation is provided in the `rule_based/` folder:

- `rule_based/R/rule_based.R` simulates one rule-based trial;
- `rule_based/R/rb_simulation.R` runs repeated simulations;
- `fig_tables/R/rb_summary.R` calculates operating-characteristic summaries;
- `fig_tables/R/tab_helpers.R` constructs comparison tables.

The rule-based design can be run using:

```{r}
#| label: run-rule-based-design
#| eval: false

rule_based_results <- run_rule_based(
  cap_method = "capped",
  generation_method = "scenarios",
  prior_spec = "id70_p",
  n_sim_scenario = 1000,
  simulation_seed = 250909,
  n_cap = 35
)
```

The same true parameter files are used for the rule-based and Bayesian CRM
designs, ensuring that both approaches are evaluated under the same
dose-response settings.

A separate posterior-updating example is not provided for the rule-based
design because it does not use a Bayesian posterior distribution.

# Simulation output files

The Bayesian CRM produces the following output files.

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `sims.csv` | Cohort-level administered doses and infection outcomes |
| `summary_stats.csv` | Posterior summaries at the most recently administered dose |
| `est.probs.csv` | Posterior infection-probability summaries at all candidate doses |
| `est.id70s.csv` | Posterior summaries of \(\log_{10}(ID_{70})\) |
| `time_exp.csv` | Total simulation computation time |

For the illustrative trial, the following additional files are generated.

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `learning_trial_dat.csv` | Cohort-level illustrative-trial data |
| `learning_post_curves.csv` | Posterior dose-response bands following each cohort |

# Operating characteristics

The simulation study evaluates:

- average and median total sample size;
- number of participants treated at the final administered dose;
- number of participants treated above the final administered dose;
- final dose-selection probabilities;
- mean bias of the posterior median of \(\log_{10}(ID_{70})\);
- mean absolute error of \(\log_{10}(ID_{70})\);
- RMSE of \(\log_{10}(ID_{70})\);
- average posterior credible-interval width; and
- coverage of the true \(\log_{10}(ID_{70})\).

The final administered dose is defined as the dose given to the final cohort.
The number treated at this dose includes all participants challenged at the
same dose throughout the trial.

# Reproducing all manuscript outputs

The selected tables and figures presented in this guide are intended to
demonstrate the main analysis workflow.

The complete manuscript and supplementary outputs can be reproduced from the
scripts and helper functions in:

```text
fig_tables/
```

The simulation models and trial-generation functions are provided in:

```text
bayesian_crm/
rule_based/
```

Because the full simulation study involves repeated Stan model fitting, the
simulation chunks are displayed with:

```yaml
eval: false
```

This allows readers to view and copy the complete code without rerunning the
computationally intensive analyses when rendering the guide.

# Reproducibility

Random-number seeds are specified for:

- generation of random true parameter values;
- selection of fixed scenarios;
- simulation of trial outcomes; and
- construction of prior-predictive figures.

The code uses `here::here()` for project-relative paths and avoids dependence
on a user-specific working directory.
